newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on wheat slide, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on wheat slide, exports.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a late collapse in wheat futures, traders said.
The market held firm most of the session on aggressive export demand for U.S. soybeans in latest weekly data and on commercial buying of the November contract, they said.

"Obviously we're firm on the sales number. The pace of usage coupled with the China sales and sales to unknown puts us ahead of last year's pace," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. "It's early to say the pattern will continue but the beans sales may mirror corn sales last year."
U.S. corn exports were very strong during 1995-96.

USDA early Thursday said the U.S. net exports of soybeans for the week ended October 17 tallied nearly 1.4 million tonnes, 20 percent above last week's marketing year high and 81 percent above the four-week average. Also that total was only six percent less than the all-time weekly record of 1,484,300 tonnes for the week ending November 12, 1987.
Traders said the market took notice of not only the weekly sales tally but was encouraged by the 287,800 tonnes sold to China and a sale of 331,600 tonnes to unknown destinations.
Soybean futures closed two to seven cents per bushel lower, with November down two at $6.96-1/2.
Traders said the tally earmarked "unknown" in USDA's weekly export sales report may end up in China or Brazil.
A Rio trader Thursday said "the talk here is crushers such as Ceval and Sadia have bought a total of five cargoes in recent weeks which would give around 300,000 tonnes."
"The demand for soybeans is continuing this week and it's quite likely Brazil is a buyer not only of soybeans but products," a cash-connected trader said.
Around 96 percent of Brazil's 1995-96 soybean crop was sold by last week, leaving only 885,000 tonnes still to be negotiated, said independent consultant Safras e Mercado in its weekly newsletter.
Wet weather in the U.S. Midwest which was slowing soybean harvesting also boosted the market as did net commercial buying and commercial bull spreading, the traders said.

Cargill Inc bought nine million bushels of November soybeans, Cargill was buying December and January soyoil and ADM Investor Services was a noted purchaser of December, January and March soymeal, traders said.
CBOT's estimated futures volume was at 80,000 contracts, up from 66,412 Wednesday.
In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 1,000 March $6.75 puts and sold 1,000 March $7.00 puts at 9-1/4 to 9-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, up from 15,111 Wednesday. Sam Nelson 312-408-8721
